item.title: Group Dynamics
item.description: Current Projects: Ethical judgement & decision-making Information sharing Ethical judgment & decision-making There is a fair amount of research on unethical behavior in and by groups (see Mannix, Neal, & Tenbrunsel, 2006, for a review). Even in situations where individuals behave cooperatively and abide by prior agreements, groups often defect from such agreements in order to protect or enhance the group (Wildschut, Pinter, Vevea, Insko, & Schopler, 2003; Morgan & Tindale, 2002).

item.title: Moral/Political
item.description: Current Projects: Moral foundations Political extremism Moral foundations The trolley problem has been used in moral psychology for its ability to capture both cognitive and emotional approaches to moral judgment. In the switch dilemma, a runaway trolley is headed for five workers who will be killed if it proceeds on its present course (Thomson, 1985). To save them, one must throw a switch, turning the trolley so it will kill one person instead of five.
